+            nn.Linear(hidden, hidden // 2),
+            nn.ReLU(),

method_selection.why: Validation primary peaks at 0.604998 around epoch 3.5, then declines while training loss continues to edge downward, indicating mild overfitting. With 23 iterations left, the coherent dropout, row-L2, AdamW, and LR-decay package has the highest honest expected gain among eligible overfit treatments and can extend useful validation learning beyond the current peak; this is materially different from the measured-dead single-dose variants.

rejected.reason: The post-peak checkpoints are already degrading, and its expected gain of at most 0.003 is lower than the compound regularization package.
A clean capacity reduction is plausible but expected to recover at most 0.003 and may introduce underfitting; the curve supports schedule-level regularization first.
It is already part of the known-best frozen stack and its measured advantage over no auxiliary training was only 0.0001, so repeating it offers little new gain.

expected_delta_basis: The parent learning curve reaches primary 0.604998 at epoch 3.5 before declining, while the journal and menu identify rapid step LR decay as the only schedule family that has beaten the 0.604-0.605 plateau.

hypothesis: Because validation primary peaks at epoch 3.5 and then falls, indicating mild overfit, adding quadratically shrunk short/long-duration residual heads around the shared DCN prediction will capture the 18-second censoring discontinuity without materially increasing effective capacity and improve validation primary by 0.0030.

+def make_pairs(users, labels, seed):

+class DurationRegimeDCN(nn.Module):

+            nn.Linear(128, 128),
+            nn.ReLU(),

+        rep_dim = input_dim + 128
+        self.shared_head = nn.Linear(rep_dim, 1)
+        self.short_residual = nn.Linear(rep_dim, 1, bias=True)
+        self.long_residual = nn.Linear(rep_dim, 1, bias=True)
+        nn.init.zeros_(self.short_residual.weight)
+        nn.init.zeros_(self.short_residual.bias)
+        nn.init.zeros_(self.long_residual.weight)
+        nn.init.zeros_(self.long_residual.bias)

+    def forward(self, x, duration_ms):
+        x0 = self.embedding(x).flatten(1)
+        cross = self.cross1(x0, x0)
+        cross = self.cross2(x0, cross)
+        deep = self.mlp(x0)
+        rep = torch.cat([cross, deep], dim=1)
+        shared = self.shared_head(rep).squeeze(1)
+        short_delta = self.short_residual(rep).squeeze(1)
+        long_delta = self.long_residual(rep).squeeze(1)
+        is_short = duration_ms <= 18000.0
+        delta = torch.where(is_short, short_delta, long_delta)

+

method_selection.citation: D2Q duration debiasing, KDD 2022 (arXiv:2206.06003); KuaiRand research notes
method_selection.why: Validation primary peaks at epoch 3.5 and then declines while training loss trends downward, indicating mild overfit. However, the overfit family is portfolio-excluded and the prior aggressive regularization package was rejected at 0.6019 versus the 0.6050 parent. Duration-regime heads are an untried, non-dead diversification with the strongest credible eligible upside (+0.002-0.006); regularizing both heads toward the shared parent limits added-capacity risk while addressing the label-regime discontinuity at 18 seconds.

rejected.reason: The relevant aggressive compound package was already rejected at 0.6019, and the overfit family is excluded from this portfolio step.
It belongs to the excluded overfit family and has lower estimated upside than duration-regime heads.
Eligible but expected gain is only +0.000-0.003 on five-item binary lists, below the honest upside of duration-regime heads.
Measured-dead at 0.5991 and therefore cannot be selected.

expected_delta_basis: The selected duration-regime-heads card estimates +0.002 to +0.006, while the parent measured primary 0.6050 and its learning curve peaks at epoch 3.5.

hypothesis: Because validation primary peaks early at epoch 3.5 and then mildly declines, indicating overfit, an EMA with decay 0.998 over training weights will average the useful near-peak trajectory and improve validation primary by approximately 0.0010.

method_selection.citation: SWA (Izmailov et al.); EMA training practice; `research/models-losses-hparams.md` seed-variance guidance
method_selection.why: Validation primary peaks at epoch 3.5 and then trends downward while training loss continues to improve, indicating mild overfit. Several late checkpoints remain close to the peak rather than collapsing, so SWA/EMA can average this useful near-peak region and reduce optimizer variance at low cost. Honest expected gain is small, about 0.000-0.003, but this is the best-fitting untried overfit intervention after the aggressive regularization package failed.

rejected.reason: The prescribed compound package was already tested in node_002 and fell from 0.6050 to 0.6019, so repeating it would ignore the journal outcome.

It is eligible but requires retraining a lower-capacity model and has similarly small expected upside; the tightly clustered near-peak checkpoints provide more direct evidence for checkpoint averaging.
The frozen known-best parent already includes the measured auxiliary setup, whose three-seed advantage was only 0.0001, so it is not a new intervention.
